claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash carries two Engram layers of roughly 384M table rows each with 256-byte FP8 entries plus ue8m0 block scales, totaling about 200 GB of table weights alone.
stance_target: The claim that Engram memory tables are far larger than GPU HBM on a 64 GB-card box
scope_conditions: vLLM v0.31.0 Engram feature docs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint
quoted_support: Engram tables dwarf typical embedding weights: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash carries two Engram layers of roughly 384M table rows each, with 256-byte FP8 entries plus their ue8m0 block scales - about 200 GB of table weights alone.

claim: vLLM's Engram CPU offload is on by default: tables live in pinned host memory and are served directly from the Triton kernel through unified virtual addressing, prefetched on a side CUDA stream to overlap with preceding layers, with freed GPU memory going to KV cache.
stance_target: Whether offloaded Engram tables can be read directly by GPU kernels without staging copies
scope_conditions: vLLM v0.31.0, cpu_offload defaults true, VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD defaults true
quoted_support: By default vLLM stores them in pinned host memory and serves lookups directly from the Triton kernel through unified virtual addressing (UVA), prefetching on a side CUDA stream so transfers overlap with the compute of preceding layers. The freed GPU memory goes to the KV cache.

claim: Engram layer layout - table sizes, n-gram size, head count - is fixed by the checkpoint and is not user-configurable in vLLM; only storage and sharding are configurable via --engram-config.
stance_target: How much freedom a practitioner has to shrink Engram tables to fit a small-VRAM box
quoted_support: The layer layout - table sizes, n-gram size, head count - is fixed by the checkpoint and is not user-configurable. Only the storage and sharding described below are configurable, via --engram-config.

claim: vLLM offers two Engram data-parallel topologies: the default keeps one TP-sharded table copy per DP replica with no cross-replica communication, while embedding_across_dp shards hash heads across all TP x DP ranks into a single table copy and exchanges rows back each step, trading per-step DP collectives for a much smaller table footprint.
stance_target: Whether Engram serving can avoid cross-GPU collectives at the cost of host memory
scope_conditions: vLLM v0.31.0, DeepSeek V4.1 Engram, embedding_across_dp setting
quoted_support: With embedding_across_dp: true, the hash heads are sharded across all TP x DP ranks into a single table copy. Each step gathers the hash ids of every co-located DP replica, each rank looks up the heads it owns, and the rows are exchanged back. This trades per-step DP collectives for a much smaller table footprint.
numbers: one table copy vs one per replica

claim: dp_shared_memory stores one copy of each TP shard in /dev/shm shared by co-located DP replicas via cudaHostRegister, dropping host memory from one table copy per replica to one per node, with no per-step Engram DP collectives.
stance_target: Whether a multi-GPU box can avoid duplicating a 200 GB table per replica
scope_conditions: vLLM v0.31.0, requires cpu_offload enabled, data_parallel_size > 1, shared IPC namespace
quoted_support: When the tables are CPU-offloaded and DP replicas are co-located on one node, dp_shared_memory stores one copy of each TP shard in /dev/shm, shared by all co-located replicas through cudaHostRegister. Each replica then prefetches only its own tokens - no per-step Engram DP collectives - and host memory drops from one table copy per replica to one per node.
numbers: one copy per node vs one per replica

claim: Engram CPU offload requires a GPU with UVA support and vLLM fails fast when it is unavailable, so the offload path is not portable to arbitrary hardware.
stance_target: Whether the offload path can be assumed to work on any GPU
quoted_support: CPU offload requires a GPU with UVA support; vLLM fails fast when it is unavailable.

claim: DeepSeek V4.1 Engram does not support DBO or microbatching in vLLM, requiring --enable-dbo to be disabled and --ubatch-size set to 0.
quoted_support: DeepSeek V4.1 Engram does not support DBO or microbatching; disable --enable-dbo and set --ubatch-size 0.
